title: Bounded linear extensions from local extendability by Zorn maximality
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a multiplicative absolute value $|\cdot|:K\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$, meaning $|a|=0$ exactly when $a=0$, $|1|=1$, and $|ab|=|a||b|$. Assume $|a+b|\leq|a|+|b|$. Let $V$ be a $K$-vector space with a norm $\|\cdot\|:V\to\mathbf R_{\geq0}$ satisfying $\|v\|=0$ exactly when $v=0$, $\|av\|=|a|\|v\|$, and $\|v+w\|\leq\|v\|+\|w\|$. Fix a real $C>0$, a linear subspace $W\subseteq V$, and a $K$-linear map $f:W\to K$ with $|f(w)|\leq C\|w\|$ for every $w\in W$. Suppose the following local extension condition holds: for every subspace $W\subseteq U\subseteq V$, every $K$-linear $g:U\to K$ with $g|_W=f$ and $|g(u)|\leq C\|u\|$ for every $u\in U$, and every $x\in V\setminus U$, there is a $K$-linear $G:U+Kx\to K$ with $G|_U=g$ and $|G(y)|\leq C\|y\|$ for every $y\in U+Kx$, where $U+Kx=\{u+ax:u\in U,\ a\in K\}$. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal P(V\times K)$ consist of the graphs of these bounded partial extensions $g$ on all subspaces $U$ containing $W$, ordered by inclusion; the graph is $\{(u,g(u)):u\in U\}$. Every nonempty chain $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S$ has $\bigcup\mathcal C\in\mathcal S$ as an upper bound, and the graph of $f$ is an upper bound for the empty chain. The family $\mathcal S$ has a maximal member, and every maximal member has domain $V$. In particular there exists a $K$-linear $h:V\to K$ with $h|_W=f$ and $|h(v)|\leq C\|v\|$ for every $v\in V$. A chain means a family whose members are pairwise comparable for inclusion; maximal means that no strictly larger member belongs to $\mathcal S$. Linearity means additivity and preservation of scalar multiplication. No completeness, closedness, nontrivial scalar absolute value, or compactness hypothesis is assumed.

proof.text: Work with the set $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal P(V\times K)$ specified in the statement. Inclusion is a partial order, since it is reflexive and transitive and mutual inclusions imply equality of sets. The graph $F$ of $f$ belongs to $\mathcal S$: its domain is $W$, it restricts to $f$, and it has the assumed bound. Thus $\mathcal S$ is nonempty, and $F$ is an upper bound for the empty chain.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion, old steps 5–6; explicit elementary chain-union and maximal-domain argument, absent from the blueprint text itself.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal S$ be a nonempty chain and put $H=\bigcup\mathcal C$, with domain $D=\{u\in V:\exists b\in K,\ (u,b)\in H\}$. If $(u,b),(u,c)\in H$, choose members $A,B\in\mathcal C$ containing these pairs. One of $A,B$ contains the other, so both pairs lie in a single function graph and $b=c$. Therefore $H$ is the graph of a function $h:D\to K$. Every member of $\mathcal C$ contains $F$; nonemptiness gives $W\subseteq D$ and $h|_W=f$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion, old steps 5–6; explicit elementary chain-union and maximal-domain argument, absent from the blueprint text itself.

proof.text: For $u,v\in D$, choose chain members whose domains contain $u,v$. The larger graph is the graph of a linear map $g$ containing both pairs $(u,h(u)),(v,h(v))$. Its domain contains $u+v$ and $au$ for every $a\in K$, and $H$ contains $(u+v,h(u)+h(v))$ and $(au,ah(u))$. By uniqueness of values in $H$, these are the additivity and scalar identities for $h$. Also $0\in W\subseteq D$, so $D$ is a subspace. Each $(u,h(u))\in H$ lies in a member graph with the fixed bound, giving $|h(u)|\leq C\|u\|$. Thus $H\in\mathcal S$ and every member of $\mathcal C$ is contained in $H$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zorn-lemma] with $X=V\times K$ and the set of subsets $\mathcal S$. Step 1 supplies an upper bound in $\mathcal S$ for the empty chain; steps 2–3 supply one for each nonempty chain. Its hypotheses hold for every chain, so it gives a maximal member of $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent scalar-extension expansion, old steps 5–6; explicit elementary chain-union and maximal-domain argument, absent from the blueprint text itself.

proof.text: Let $M$ be any maximal member, the graph of $g:U\to K$. If $U\ne V$, choose $x\in V\setminus U$. Membership $M\in\mathcal S$ gives $W\subseteq U$, $g|_W=f$, and the fixed bound, so the local extension hypothesis gives a bounded linear $G:U+Kx\to K$ extending $g$. Its graph belongs to $\mathcal S$ and contains $M$. It strictly contains $M$: it contains $(x,G(x))$, since $x=0+1x$, while $x\notin U$. This contradicts maximality. Hence every maximal member has domain $V$. Apply this to the member from step 4; its map $h$ has $h|_W=f$ and $|h(v)|\leq C\|v\|$ by membership in $\mathcal S$.

lean.statement: theorem bounded_extension_zorn {K : Type u} [Field K] {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] (abv : AbsoluteValue K ℝ≥0) (ν : V → ℝ≥0) (hνzero : ∀ v : V, ν v = 0 ↔ v = 0) (hνsmul : ∀ (a : K) (v : V), ν (a • v) = abv a * ν v) (hνadd : ∀ v w : V, ν (v + w) ≤ ν v + ν w) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C) (W : Submodule K V) (f : W →ₗ[K] K) (hf : ∀ w : W, (abv (f w) : ℝ) ≤ C * (ν (w : V) : ℝ)) (hext : ∀ (U : Submodule K V) (hWU : W ≤ U) (g : U →ₗ[K] K), g.comp (Submodule.inclusion hWU) = f → (∀ u : U, (abv (g u) : ℝ) ≤ C * (ν (u : V) : ℝ)) → ∀ x : V, x ∉ U → ∃ G : ↥(U ⊔ Submodule.span K {x}) →ₗ[K] K, G.comp (Submodule.inclusion le_sup_left) = g ∧ ∀ y : ↥(U ⊔ Submodule.span K {x}), (abv (G y) : ℝ) ≤ C * (ν (y : V) : ℝ)) : (∀ c : Set (Set (V × K)), c ⊆ boundedExtensionGraphs abv ν C W f → IsChain (· ⊆ ·) c → c.Nonempty → ⋃₀ c ∈ boundedExtensionGraphs abv ν C W f ∧ ⋃₀ c ∈ upperBounds c) ∧ (((LinearPMap.mk W f).graph : Set (V × K)) ∈ boundedExtensionGraphs abv ν C W f ∧ ((LinearPMap.mk W f).graph : Set (V × K)) ∈ upperBounds (∅ : Set (Set (V × K)))) ∧ (∃ M : Set (V × K), Maximal (· ∈ boundedExtensionGraphs abv ν C W f) M) ∧ (∀ M : Set (V × K), Maximal (· ∈ boundedExtensionGraphs abv ν C W f) M → Prod.fst '' M = Set.univ) ∧ (∃ h : V →ₗ[K] K, h.comp W.subtype = f ∧ ∀ v : V, (abv (h v) : ℝ) ≤ C * (ν v : ℝ))
